get.description: Returns the normalised code, the discount percentage, the catalogue price, the discount and what the parent would actually pay — already computed, so the client never reproduces the rounding (the discount is rounded UP, and `discountAmount` plus `finalPrice` always equals `originalPrice` exactly). The code is trimmed and upper-cased before lookup, so `  promo10 ` and `PROMO10` are the same code. **This call RESERVES NOTHING and is NOT a guarantee.** It writes no row and holds no redemption slot: it is an accurate answer about right now, not a promise about the moment of payment. The code is re-validated from scratch when the payment is created, and a code that has run out in between will be refused there. **Do NOT call this on every keystroke.** It reserves nothing, but it is not free: the route carries no throttle tier of its own, so it shares the global limit of **100 requests per minute per IP, per route**, and NAT-shared egress (schools, carrier CGNAT) means several parents spend that one bucket between them. Debounce the promo field by at least **500 ms** after the last keystroke, and prefer calling when the field loses focus or the entered code is plausibly complete. A client that ignores this gets 429 `RATE_LIMITED` on a lookup that costs one indexed read.

info.title: Oila 360 API
info.description: Main backend API (https://api.oila360.uz/docs/api.json), merged with the high-frequency device-telemetry ingest service (https://api.oila360.uz/docs/ingestion.json). Captured live 2026-09-24. Both documents sit behind HTTP basic auth. On the one schema name both documents define (AppUsageStatDto: same fields, different prose) the ingestion copy is kept, because it is the one the device surface returns.

lastSeenAt.description: Last CONTACT from the handset — a status post, a location batch, or the 15-minute usage report. Liveness, not the position’s age.

diagnostics.description: Why this handset can or cannot do what you expect (D-102) — granted permissions, special access, and device-wide settings that are not permissions (the GPS master switch, iOS Background App Refresh). Possible keys: location, locationBackground, locationServices, batteryOptimization, backgroundRefresh, usageAccess, accessibility, overlay, notifications, microphone, camera, autoStart, lowPowerMode. PARTIAL by construction: a handset reports only the keys its platform and build measure, and a MISSING key means “never reported”, NOT “denied” — render it as unknown or hide it, never as a fault. `null` (the whole map) = the child build predates diagnostics.

diagnosticsAt.description: When the map above was last written. Separates “never reported” (`null`) from “reported and all fine” (a full map of `granted`), which the map alone cannot express.

memberId.description: The owning parent. Always your own member id on this surface.

profilePictureFileId.description: Internal file id behind `profilePictureUrl`; clients use the URL.

profilePictureUrl.description: STABLE public URL, safe to cache (D-048) — not a signed, expiring one.

dsn.description: Serial of the attached handset. `null` = no handset attached.

timezone.description: IANA zone captured at pairing. Drives lock schedules and the usage day.

fcmToken.description: FCM token of the attached handset. Present for internal use; ignore it.

pairedAt.description: `null` = no handset attached. This is the flag to render "not connected" on, and the reason an unpaired child is never probed.

manualLockEnabled.description: Derived (D-122): true only while a manual lock is running — `startsAt ≤ now < endsAt`. A manual lock that has not started yet, or has ended, reads false.

manualLock.description: The manual lock (D-122) while its end is still ahead — a running one or one that has not started yet — so the app can show "locked until 16:00". `null` = none, or it has ended.

status.description: Last-known telemetry. `null` = the handset has never reported. This read fires NO liveness probe (D-094) — open the child’s detail for that.

ts.description: When this FIX was captured — NOT `lastSeenAt`. A stationary child legitimately has an old `ts` and a fresh `lastSeenAt`; render the pin’s age from this one.

memberId.description: The owning parent. Always your own member id on this surface.

profilePictureFileId.description: Internal file id behind `profilePictureUrl`; clients use the URL.

profilePictureUrl.description: STABLE public URL, safe to cache (D-048) — not a signed, expiring one.

dsn.description: Serial of the attached handset. `null` = no handset attached.

timezone.description: IANA zone captured at pairing. Drives lock schedules and the usage day.

fcmToken.description: FCM token of the attached handset. Present for internal use; ignore it.

pairedAt.description: `null` = no handset attached. This is the flag to render "not connected" on, and the reason an unpaired child is never probed.

manualLockEnabled.description: Derived (D-122): true only while a manual lock is running — `startsAt ≤ now < endsAt`. A manual lock that has not started yet, or has ended, reads false.

manualLock.description: The manual lock (D-122) while its end is still ahead — a running one or one that has not started yet — so the app can show "locked until 16:00". `null` = none, or it has ended.

status.description: Last-known telemetry. `null` = the handset has never reported. This read fires NO liveness probe (D-094) — open the child’s detail for that.

location.description: The freshest STORED fix. `null` = never reported. Reading this endpoint also fires a liveness probe at the handset (60s cooldown per child); a reply arrives later as a `device:status` WS frame carrying these same `status` + `location` members, so swap it in without reshaping. No frame means nothing at all — keep rendering these values. NOTE: a probe reply does not currently refresh `location`; the handset answers with battery/network/ringer only.

deviceId.description: Null for notices about the member rather than a handset (subscription, payment).

occurredAt.description: OCCURRENCE time: when the event happened (for a zone crossing, the fix’s own time). ISO-8601 UTC, never null. Equals `createdAt` for events with no time of their own. Show this as the notification’s time, but keep the server’s order (D-116).

createdAt.description: ARRIVAL time: when the server wrote the row. The feed is ordered by it, so a late notification is on page one even when `occurredAt` is hours earlier.

items.description: Newest ARRIVAL first: `createdAt` desc, then `occurredAt` desc, then `id` desc (D-116).

startsAt.description: UTC ISO-8601 instant. Required unless `enabled` is sent.

endsAt.description: UTC ISO-8601 instant, after `startsAt` and at most 8h later.

enabled.description: Legacy toggle for the current parent app. `true` = a lock from now to now + 8h; `false` = clear the manual lock. Refused together with `startsAt`/`endsAt`.

manualLockEnabled.description: True only while the manual lock is running: `startsAt ≤ now < endsAt`.

manualLock.description: The window while its end is still ahead (a future one included), else `null`.

usageDate.description: Today by the DEVICE-LOCAL calendar (`Device.timezone`, captured at pairing) — not the server day. Limits reset at the child’s midnight.

usedSeconds.description: What the server holds for this package on `usageDate`, after this report.

dailyLimitSeconds.description: Parent-set daily limit. `null` = no limit configured for this app.

remainingSeconds.description: Floored at 0. `null` when `dailyLimitSeconds` is null, never a misleading 0.

isLimitReached.description: True once `usedSeconds >= dailyLimitSeconds`. Always false when there is no limit.

isLocked.description: Locked right now: manual lock running OR a schedule active. Kept for old child builds; a new build enforces from `manualLock` and `schedules` by its own clock instead.

manualLockEnabled.description: True only while the manual lock is running.

manualLock.description: The manual lock while its end is still ahead — a future one included, so an offline handset can lock at `startsAt` and unlock at `endsAt` by its own clock. `null` = none.

serverTime.description: The server's clock when this was read, to detect a changed handset clock.

code.description: The code as it is stored and advertised — trimmed and upper-cased. Echoed so the screen can show the canonical form of whatever the parent typed.

discountPercent.description: The discount percentage, 1–99. For the badge; the sums below are done.

originalPrice.description: The catalogue price of the chosen option, in integer UZS — read from the catalogue, not from the request.

discountAmount.description: What comes off, in integer UZS. Rounded UP, so a fractional so’m goes to the parent.

finalPrice.description: What the parent would pay, in integer UZS. Always exactly `originalPrice − discountAmount`, so the two integers reconcile against the catalogue price with no rounding of your own.

mode.description: audio = mic only, video = camera + mic

delivered.description: Whether FCM accepted the push. FALSE is a soft failure: stream.* has no poll fallback, so the device will never hear the command — fail fast, do not wait. TRUE does NOT mean the child is publishing yet.

transport.description: Informational only. 'poll' is a lie for stream.* (there is no stream-command poll endpoint) — it is reused because DispatchResult allows only these three. Switch on `delivered` alone.

room.description: Server-derived LiveKit room. Join this — never re-derive it client-side.

maxDurationSeconds.description: Server-owned lease. The child stops publishing when it expires; re-POST /stream/start at roughly half this to renew while the live screen is open.

delivered.description: Whether FCM accepted the push. FALSE is a soft failure: stream.* has no poll fallback, so the device will never hear the command — fail fast, do not wait. TRUE does NOT mean the child is publishing yet.

transport.description: Informational only. 'poll' is a lie for stream.* (there is no stream-command poll endpoint) — it is reused because DispatchResult allows only these three. Switch on `delivered` alone.

room.description: Server-derived LiveKit room. Join this — never re-derive it client-side.

lastMessageId.description: Read up to and including this message id

name.description: Re-read on every call. Do NOT cache the pairing response’s copy — a parent can rename the child or change the photo at any time, and this endpoint is how the handset learns.

profileColor.description: Hex colour for the avatar fallback.

avatarEmoji.description: Rendered over `profileColor` when there is no photo.

profilePictureUrl.description: STABLE public URL, safe to cache and reuse (D-048) — not a signed, expiring one. `null` = no photo set; fall back to `avatarEmoji` + `profileColor`.

usedSeconds.description: Device-wide total across every app for `date`. Identical to `GET /device/apps/screen-time` — one shared computation backs both, so do not recompute it from `UsageStatsManager` locally.

dailyScreenLimitSeconds.description: The parent’s daily budget, DISPLAY-ONLY — nothing enforces it. `null` = no budget set.

remainingSeconds.description: Floored at 0. `null` when no budget is set — render “no limit”, not “0 left”.

rewardPoints.description: Stars this task is worth when completed.

status.description: Only `Active` may be completed by the child. Show the “done” affordance on `Active` alone — an `Expired` or `Cancelled` task is not actionable.

totalPoints.description: The star badge — sum of `rewardPoints` across this child’s Completed tasks.

recent.description: The newest tasks only (at most 2), every status included, newest first. This is the home card’s preview — use `GET /device/tasks` for the full paginated list.

text.description: `null` on an image-only message (`hasAttachment: true`) and on a System row (`systemKind` set) — render from those instead of showing an empty line.

hasAttachment.description: Whether the message carries an image. No URL here — fetch one when opened.

systemKind.description: Set on System rows (e.g. an SOS press); render localized copy from it.

unreadCount.description: Parent-sent messages past this child’s read watermark. System rows are addressed to the parent and never counted here.

lastMessage.description: `null` when the thread has no messages — or does not exist yet.

unpairPinRequired.description: Whether a parent PIN gates this child’s self-unpair. `true` — the disconnect screen asks for it and sends `pin` to `POST /device/unpair`. `false` — show NO keypad, just a confirmation: with no PIN set the unpair succeeds on any four digits, so a keypad here would accept whatever was typed. Re-read on every call: it flips as soon as the parent sets a PIN, with no re-pair and no app restart.

durationMonths.description: Gift: required. Sale: required unless durationDays is given. May be a duration the catalogue does not sell.

durationDays.description: Sale only, instead of durationMonths: the period length in days.

amount.description: Sale only, and required there: what the parent paid, in integer UZS.

storeReviewMode.description: True only when this exact platform/build pair is the one an operator recorded as under store review, the master toggle is on, and any configured expiry is still in the future. Treat any error or timeout as FALSE.

enabled.description: The master toggle, exactly as an operator left it

iosBuild.description: The iOS review build, or null

androidBuild.description: The Android review build (versionCode), or null

expiresAt.description: Null means it never expires on its own

expired.description: Derived, never stored: true when a configured expiry has already passed. This is why review mode can stop taking effect while `enabled` still reads true — the server never rewrites the operator’s own setting.

updatedByAdminId.description: The operator who last saved. Resolve the name through the audit log — `GET /admin/audit-logs?action=STORE_REVIEW_CONFIG_UPDATED` carries the username.

updatedAt.description: Null when nothing has ever been saved

version.description: The bundle’s identity on an install. Burned forever — deleting this bundle does not free the string for a second artefact.

checksum.description: SHA-256 hex of the archive. The plugin verifies it after downloading, so a truncated or swapped file is discarded rather than run.

url.description: Derived from the stored object at read time, never a stored column — it stays correct when the storage driver changes. Fetching it returns exactly the bytes uploaded.

isActive.description: Always false on upload. Uploading is not publishing — a bundle sits inert until an operator deliberately activates it.

uploadedByAdminId.description: The operator who uploaded. Null only if that account was ever hard-deleted.

uploadedByUsername.description: The uploader’s name, so a release nobody remembers making can be asked about without a second lookup. Null when the account was hard-deleted.

ts.description: Device-side capture time. MUST be a UTC ISO-8601 instant ending in `Z` — a zoneless string is rejected. Past timestamps are kept as-is (an offline backlog is normal); a timestamp more than 60s in the future is clamped to server time and excluded from geofencing, which means a wrong handset clock silently loses crossings.

accepted.description: Rows written. Always equals `items.length` on success — a future-dated fix is NOT rejected, it is clamped to server time and still counted here (it is only excluded from geofencing). So this is a write receipt, not a validation result: do not diff it against what you sent to decide whether to resend.

battery.description: Charge percentage, 0–100. Crossing the low threshold alerts the parent once.

diagnostics.description: Why this handset can or cannot do what the parent expects (D-102): granted permissions, special access, and device-wide settings that are not permissions at all (the GPS master switch, iOS Background App Refresh). Known keys: location, locationBackground, locationServices, batteryOptimization, backgroundRefresh, usageAccess, accessibility, overlay, notifications, microphone, camera, autoStart, lowPowerMode. Send only the keys this platform and build actually measure — an omitted key means "never reported" and is merged over the stored value, never treated as denied. An unknown key rejects the whole request, so the server always ships before a build that adds one.

updated.description: Always `true` — the snapshot is persisted. Carries no state back: the battery-low alert and the parent-facing `device:status` frame are server-side side-effects the child never sees.

name.description: User-visible label, for the parent’s list.

items.description: The FULL current installed set. Anything previously installed and missing here is flagged uninstalled, so a partial payload silently removes the rest.

synced.description: Packages upserted. Counts DISTINCT package names, so a payload that repeats one reports it once — this can be lower than `items.length` without anything failing.

removed.description: Packages that were installed and are absent from this payload; flagged uninstalled, NOT deleted, so the parent’s lock/limit survives a reinstall (D-037). Send the FULL installed set every time — a partial sync marks everything you omitted as removed.

usedSeconds.description: Seconds used SINCE THE LAST REPORT, not the running total — the server adds this to the device-local day. Sending a total re-adds it every cycle.

lockedPackages.description: The FULL effectively-blocked set for this device right now — parent-locked apps plus apps over today’s limit. Enforce exactly this list and drop whatever you were enforcing before; it is not a delta, and it covers apps absent from your payload.

stats.description: One line per DISTINCT package in your payload — nothing else. It is the reply to what you just reported, not the device’s whole day; use `GET /device/apps/screen-time` for the device-wide total.

usedSeconds.description: Seconds this app was on screen on `date`, counted from that day’s local midnight — the day’s figure so far, NOT the seconds since your last report. It replaces what the server holds for this app on that day.

date.description: The handset’s local calendar day, YYYY-MM-DD. A day outside [today − 7, today + 1] (today by the child profile’s timezone) is skipped, not rejected.

items.description: Every app with screen time on `date`; a package appears at most once. An app left out reads 0 for that day, and `[]` says the day had no screen time at all.

days.description: One entry per local day, each date at most once. Today plus up to 7 days back.

lockedPackages.description: The FULL effectively-blocked set for this device right now — parent-locked apps plus apps over today’s limit, judged on today’s figures after this report was written. Enforce exactly this list and drop whatever you were enforcing before.

stats.description: One line per package in TODAY’s entry of your report, and nothing else. Empty when the report has no entry for today (by `Device.timezone`) — earlier days get no lines.

usedSeconds.description: Device-wide total across every app for `date`. Server-summed from the same rows the parent’s summary reads, so the two surfaces cannot disagree — do not recompute it from `UsageStatsManager` locally.

dailyScreenLimitSeconds.description: The parent’s daily budget, DISPLAY-ONLY — nothing enforces it. `null` = no budget set.

remainingSeconds.description: Floored at 0. `null` when no budget is set — render “no limit”, not “0 left”.

packageName.description: The app the removal was attempted on — usually this app itself.

applicationName.description: User-visible label; goes straight into the parent’s notification copy.

reported.description: Always `true` — the report was accepted. It does NOT mean the parent has been notified: the alert rides a durable queue and the feed row + push are written by the other service moments later.
